newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ford Mexico hopes for quick end to stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Ford Mexico hopes for quick end to stoppage.

text.p: Ford de Mexico, a subsidiary of Ford Motor Co hopes to reach an agreement with workers that could allow its idled Cuautitlan plant to resume operations as soon as Thursday, a company spokesman said.

Workers at all three Ford plants in Mexico began walking off the job on Friday after the company said Ford de Mexico posted losses in 1996 and would not be offering profit-sharing checks. Workers have returned to all but the Cuautitlan plant.
"We hope to reach an agreement today," company spokesman Carlos Hernandez told Reuters. "We are trying to negotiate. If (the union demand) is reasonable, maybe something can happen."

The Hermosillo assembly plant was closed Friday afternoon and Monday before the workers returned on Tuesday, costing the company output of about 1,000 Ford Escort and Mercury Tracer models, primarily for export to the United States and Canada.
At the Chihuahua motor plant, workers held out Monday afternoon and Tuesday, but returned to work on Wednesday, causing lost output of some 2,000 motors.

The only plant that remains idle is is Cuautitlan just north of Mexico City, where Ford produces 468 units a day of the Ford Contour, Mercury Mystique and F-series pickup models for both the national and export markets.
Cuautitlan workers have stayed off the job since Monday afternoon, Hernandez said, meaning lost output could top 1,000 units by the end of Wednesday.
Ford de Mexico reported 1996 losses of 1.657 billion pesos, or about $207 million. Under Mexican law, companies must return at least eight percent of after-tax profits to workers in May of each year.
Ford de Mexico posted a loss in 1994, but in 1995 offered workers a bonus of 1,500 pesos anyway.
"The union is asking for some similar kind of bonus," Hernandez said.
Earlier Wednesday, one union leader in Hermosillo told Reuters workers would hold a general assembly on Friday if the issue wasn't resolved and that they were prepared to again walk off the job.
